note: Magical power granted by one accessory, by rarity. Hand-entered: the items resource exposes an accessory's rarity but not its magical power. Everything else in the accessory model is API-derived.

excludedItems.note: Empty on purpose. Several bag items (party hats, cake bag) are classified ACCESSORY by the items resource, and nothing in the API says whether they grant magical power. Excluding them on a hunch would hide buyable XP; the computed-vs-reported MP readout is the check instead.

knownGaps: highest_magical_power is a high-water mark, not a current reading, so computed MP can sit below it legitimately.

All three special cases are modelled now: Hegemony doubles its own MP, an Abicase adds 1 per 2 Abiphone contacts, and an imbued Rift Prism is worth 11 whether or not it is still in the bag (the profile records it as rift.access.consumed_prism, since imbuing consumes it).

Contacts are counted from active_contacts, not contact_data. The two disagree: contact_data holds only the contacts with state attached and read 80 against a real 84 on the profile this was checked against, which is 2 MP.

Measured against a maxed profile (2,122 MP in game) the model reaches 2,091. Of the residual 31, one part is known — a Balloon Hat 2024 the player wears that the items resource does not carry at all, at any category, so it has no rarity and no magical power we can defend. The rest is unexplained. Ruled out by measurement rather than by argument: dungeon accessories counting double (that overshoots to 2,216), enrichments (the wiki's Enrichments page never mentions magical power), families scoring below their own ceiling (none do), and Personal Deletor 6000 vs 7000 being separate families (the wiki states 7000 upgrades_from 6000, so merging them is right).

Accessories whose rarity climbs through play — Book of Progression, Pandora's Box, Runebook — are COMMON in the items resource and much higher in the bag. Reading the item's own lore fixes this for what a player holds, but the model still prices the *unowned* ones off the resource, so their share of the ceiling is understated.
